factors: Long-form 85-minute creator account with multiple security and reliability claims.
Comparing reported productivity scale with actual code and permission boundaries requires several evidence classes.
complexity.rationale: An extended treatment is warranted by the long source, nine claim cues, conditional adoption decisions and unverified operational outcome claims.

sourceMap.rationale: Task-sized sessions reduce context drift; no controlled outcome comparison.
Separate model review finds possible omissions; agreement is not proof.
Five-perspective review pattern; public total-review skill includes inappropriate unrestricted review permissions.
Independent bounded tasks can use child agents; efficiency not independently measured.
Cloud-local sandbox and Mac relay require separate authorization and identity boundaries.
Scheduled loops run in fresh contexts; website scheduler and secrets behavior matter.
High autonomous run volume and unattended percentage are speaker self-report, not outcome audit.
Proposed safe autonomy versus human approval is a design rule, not measured universal proportion.
Recurring interventions can become a read-only scan recipe with deduplication and exit condition.

sourceCoverage.rationale: The independent reviewer inspected nine caption cue windows and four video frames; these corroborate bounded article claims. Continuous full-length audiovisual verification was not performed.

supportingArgument.rationale: Narrow sessions, cross-model critical review and read-only loops are supported as described methods by the creator's video and public instructions.

evidenceRoles.rationale: Private automatic captions are timing aids; first-party public source code confirms mechanisms; reported scale and outcomes remain self-report.

counterargument.rationale: A high volume of sessions is not an outcome, and an unrestricted review permission profile undermines the claimed separation of review and execution.

tradeoffs.rationale: Fresh short sessions reduce drift but add coordination overhead, while cloud loops offer continuity at the cost of hosted scheduling and Mac access exposure.

falsifiability.rationale: The proposed ten-run intervention scan can fail if findings repeat, attention cost rises or a permission boundary is crossed.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The editorial contribution separates agent work throughput from durable authorization and outcome evidence, and recommends one bounded adoption pilot.

performance.rationale: Creator-displayed loop counts and session totals are distinguished from unmeasured accepted completion, defects, and productivity; no external audit is claimed.

economics.rationale: The article identifies hosting, subscription, intervention and operating-cost unknowns and proposes a bounded local comparison, not fabricated cost conclusions.

threatGovernance.rationale: Default-all loop secrets, remote Mac execution and unrestricted review instructions warrant least-privilege rejection before any deployment.

gaps.rationale: Review relied on timestamped caption passages and four sampled frames, not continuous audiovisual playback; uncertain demonstrations retain explicit attribution.
Creator activity and autonomy counts are self-reports and not independently audited; the article does not present them as verified outcomes.
No controlled Cloudroom-versus-GhostMesh benchmark has run. The article presents that as a proposed experiment, not an observed result.

decisionRationale: Independent source, copy, and privacy review accepted the qualified article for Tony's exact-hash editorial decision. No substantive rewrite was requested; public release still requires the authenticated owner PR marker and separate exact-head authorization.
